$comment: Lumos pinned toolchain manifest. Produced by WP-01 slice S0. Consumed by the bootstrap scripts of TRS-REP-006 (WP-01 slice S7) and by the clean-container CI evidence job. Every version here is one that was installed and executed on the authoring host; nothing is aspirational.

host.host_note: Authoring host moved at WP-03 S0 (owner handover 2026-11-19) from the Windows 11 laptop to the Linux cloud container. CI remains the prover; this records where authoring-time verification now runs. Prior hosts: Windows 11 Enterprise 10.0.26200 amd64 (WP-01..WP-02).

go.why: Single-generator rule (TRS Sec. 18.4): /tools/vectorgen and the backend conformance runner 'go test ./protocol/...' are Go.

jdk.license_note: Standard OpenJDK licensing. Build toolchain only; not linked into any shipped artefact. Installed on explicit owner instruction.
jdk.why: TRS Sec. 5.3 mandated a Java 17 toolchain; CR-002 (accepted 2026-08-19, executed in WP-02 slice S5) moves it to Java 21 LTS so lazysodium-android 5.2.0 can be read and its 16 KB-aligned natives taken. Drives the pure-JVM :protocol-conformance module, the Android module and every JVM job in CI.
jdk.superseded: Was 17.0.20+8 (Eclipse Temurin) from WP-01 slice S5 until CR-002. The predecessor is named rather than deleted because the 17 pin is what several build-file comments and the Checkstyle 12.x hold were reasoning about.
jdk.language_level_note: The TOOLCHAIN is 21; the Android module still COMPILES to Java 17 language level (compileOptions in android-app/app/build.gradle.kts). CR-002 needed a javac that can read bytecode-65 class files, which is a property of the JDK and not of -source/-target. Raising what the app emits is a separate change, deferred to WP-03.

node.install: preinstalled in the Claude cloud authoring container
node.why: admin-console empty-shell build (TypeScript, ESLint + tsc strict) in slice S7.
node.version_note: This entry records the AUTHORING HOST, which moved a second time at WP-03 S0 (owner handover 2026-11-19): from the Windows laptop (v26.7.0) to the Linux cloud authoring container (v22.23.5 LTS). The CI pin is separate and deliberately stays on the 24 LTS line: both workflows set node-version '24', and @types/node 24.x in admin-console describes that runtime. Moving CI is a TRS-CICD-006 controlled update, not a side effect of the host moving. Earlier hosts are named in the history rather than deleted: laptop v26.7.0 (WP-02), laptop v24.19.0 (WP-01).

swift.why: Swift 6 / SwiftPM is not installable on this Windows host in a form that satisfies the WP-01 known trap: LumosProtocolConformance must run on a macOS CI host without a simulator. The Swift conformance runner is authored in slice S5 and executed on a GitHub Actions macos-latest runner, path-filtered per owner instruction to protocol/, test-vectors/ and the iOS conformance target only.

android_sdk.note: TRS Sec. 5.3 baseline compileSdk/targetSdk 36 is satisfied by android-36 + build-tools 36.1.0. cmdline-tools is absent; CI license acceptance and headless SDK management are addressed in slice S7.

cmdline_tools_resolution.authoring_host: still absent. tools/bootstrap reports it as MISSING with the exact remediation rather than downloading it: the archive comes from a licence-gated Google endpoint and accepting an SDK licence is the developer's act, not a script's.
cmdline_tools_resolution.ci: android-actions/setup-android provisions cmdline-tools and accepts the licences on the runner, so the Android shell build never depends on the authoring host's SDK state.
cmdline_tools_resolution.verified: The Android shell was built on the authoring host with the pre-existing platform 36 + build-tools 36.1.0 (assembleDevDebug, assembleProdRelease, lintDevDebug all succeeded). CI reproduces the build from a provisioned SDK.

gh.why: Opens and updates the per-slice pull requests. Authenticated interactively by the owner; the agent never handles the token and never reads it out of the credential store.

gitleaks.license_verified: MIT License, Copyright (c) 2019 Zachary Rice - read from the LICENSE file shipped inside the installed package, not assumed.
gitleaks.why: Secret scan over the full git history (TRS-REP-005, TRS-CICD-001). CI tooling only; never linked into any artefact.
gitleaks.verified: Run on the authoring host against the working tree and against `git --log-opts='--all --full-history'` (23 commits): no leaks. The configuration's own rules were exercised against planted fixtures before being trusted.

gradle.note: Committed wrapper with distributionSha256Sum pinned. The published checksum was fetched from services.gradle.org and verified against the downloaded distribution BEFORE it was used to generate the wrapper.

python.note: Not a project dependency and not required by any build. Used only to read the baselined specification PDFs (pypdf 6.15.0, BSD-3-Clause). Must not appear in any lockfile or bootstrap script.

go_dependencies.note: Go module dependencies are locked in go.mod + go.sum (checksummed, 'go mod verify' green). Added as needed per slice with owner approval; this list mirrors the lockfile for auditability.

modules.why: ChaCha20-Poly1305 (IETF) AEAD per ADR-001; the Go standard library provides X25519, Ed25519, HKDF-SHA-256 and SHA-256 but not this AEAD. Owner-approved for WP-01 slice S4b.

not_yet_pinned.note: Slice S7 closed the outstanding lockfile items per TRS-REP-003. tools/deplock asserts by test that nothing listed here is in fact already pinned, so this list cannot quietly become wrong in either direction.

resolved_in_s7.agp: gradle/libs.versions.toml pins androidGradlePlugin 9.3.1; see build_dependencies below.
resolved_in_s7.npm_lockfile: admin-console/package-lock.json committed at lockfileVersion 3; every entry carries a sha512 integrity hash and npm ci verifies it.
resolved_in_s7.sbom: tools/sbomgen emits evidence/sbom/lumos-sbom.json (CycloneDX 1.5). A STUB, and it says so in its own metadata: direct dependencies only, no transitive closure, no provenance. The release SBOM is WP-11's.

owner_ruled_pending.note: Empty. The Lazysodium adoption that lived here from WP-02 S2 was carried out in WP-02 S4b, on the condition it was recorded under: the first slice that executes identity-grade crypto on a device. See runtime_dependencies below.

not_applicable.note: Empty. The SwiftPM entry that lived here - 'the package declares no external dependencies, so there is nothing to pin' - expired in WP-02 S4b when swift-sodium was adopted. Package.resolved is now committed and the swift job verifies the resolved revision against it.

resolved_in_s4b.lazysodium_android: Adopted at 5.1.0 under the owner's approval of 2026-08-18. Conditions and their evidence: UNMODIFIED USE - one file, LibsodiumRecoveryCrypto.java, imports it at all; LICENCE TEXT IN THE APP'S THIRD-PARTY NOTICES - docs/legal/third-party-notices.md, shipped as an APK asset rather than left in docs/; SBOM - evidence/sbom/lumos-sbom.json; TOOLCHAIN MANIFEST - this entry; IF PATCHING IS EVER NEEDED - switch to a direct libsodium JNI binding rather than fork, recorded here so the condition survives the conversation it was given in.
resolved_in_s4b.swift_sodium: Adopted at 0.11.0 (ISC) under the same approval. Only the Clibsodium product is taken.

static_analysis.note: The TRS-CODE-006 analyser stack, added in WP-02 slice S0. Every entry is pinned, and the pin is asserted against this file by tools/staticanalysis. Three of the six carry copyleft licences and are flagged accordingly per AGENTS.md Sec. 3: all are CI analysers that read source and emit reports. None is linked into, bundled with or distributed alongside any artefact, and none places an obligation on the code it analyses. TRS-CODE-006 names each of these tools by name, so the requirement itself is the approval record.

modules.license_note: Copyleft-family, flagged explicitly. Build-time analyser only; never distributed.
modules.why: Java source rules of TRS Sec. 24: the TRS-CODE-004 file and complexity budgets, TRS-CODE-002 public-API Javadoc, TRS-CODE-008 error handling and TRS-CODE-007 naming.
modules.version_note: Raised from 12.3.1 at WP-03 S0 on the owner ruling of 2026-08-19 (WP-02 boundary audit): CR-002's Java 21 toolchain removed the JVM incompatibility that held 12.x ('Checkstyle 13.10.0 is not compatible with the configured JVM (17)'). 13.11.0 was executed against both Java modules under the existing explicit checkstyle.xml with zero violations - the config enumerates its rules rather than inheriting defaults, so the 13.x default-set changes introduce nothing silently; any new rule is adopted by editing the config, which is a reviewed change.

modules.license_note: Copyleft-family, flagged explicitly. Build-time analyser only; never distributed.
modules.why: Bytecode defect analysis for the Java half of TRS-CODE-006. Found the Frame payload aliasing (EI_EXPOSE_REP/EI_EXPOSE_REP2) on its first run.
modules.effort: max, report level low - the settings under which SpotBugs reports everything it is willing to say.

modules.why: Gradle integration for SpotBugs. Registers the spotbugsMain/spotbugsTest tasks the staticAnalysis task depends on.

Swift source rules of TRS Sec. 24, run with --strict so a warning fails the job. Installed from the pinned portable_swiftlint.zip release rather than the macOS runner image's preinstalled copy, whose version changes whenever the image is rebuilt.

modules.license_note: COPYLEFT, and the strongest licence in this repository. Flagged prominently. It is a standalone CI binary: invoked as a process, never imported, never linked and never shipped, and GPL-3.0 places no obligation on the Go sources it reads. TRS-CODE-006 names golangci-lint explicitly, which is the requirement-level approval for it; the owner's WP-02 S0 instruction names it again.
modules.why: Go analyser stack of TRS-CODE-006. Enabled linters map one-to-one onto TRS Sec. 24 clauses; see .golangci.yml, where each carries the requirement it serves.
Already pinned for the admin console in npm_dependencies above; listed here too because TRS-CODE-006 counts it as a member of the analyser stack and the stack should be readable in one place.

not_pinned_by_version.android_lint: Ships inside the Android Gradle Plugin and is versioned with it (androidGradlePlugin 9.3.1 in build_dependencies below). It is configured in android-app/app/build.gradle.kts with warningsAsErrors = true.
not_pinned_by_version.swift_6_strict_concurrency: A compiler mode, not a tool: Package.swift puts every target in .swiftLanguageMode(.v6) and the macOS CI job builds with -Xswiftc -warnings-as-errors. Its version is the Swift toolchain's, which is the macos-latest image's.

build_dependencies.note: Build-time plugins. Not linked into any shipped artefact, but they determine what is produced, so they are pinned and declared like any other dependency.

modules.why: Android Gradle Plugin for the app shell. AGP 8.13.0 was tried first and rejected at build time: it calls org.gradle.api.problems.internal.InternalProblems, a Gradle internal removed in Gradle 9.6.0. Bumping AGP was the right fix over downgrading the checksum-pinned Gradle 9.7.0 wrapper.

npm_dependencies.note: admin-console, devDependencies only - the WP-01 shell ships no runtime dependency. Locked in admin-console/package-lock.json with sha512 integrity per package.

modules.why: Strict-mode type checking for the admin console shell (TRS Sec. 5.3).
Lint stage for TypeScript sources (TRS-CICD-001), run with --max-warnings=0.
modules.version_note: Held on the 9.x line. 9.15.0 was tried first and rejected: npm audit reported two low-severity ReDoS advisories (GHSA-xffm-g5w8-qvg7) in the transitive @eslint/plugin-kit, fixed at 9.39.5. ESLint 10 is available but is a major bump with flat-config changes and no security motive, so it is a WP-11 dependency-automation decision, not a WP-01 one.

modules.why: ESLint's own recommended rule set, required by the flat config. Held in lockstep with eslint.
TypeScript parser and rules for ESLint 9 flat config.
Type definitions for the node:test runner the shell's tests use; no test framework is added.
modules.version_note: Moved from 22.x to 24.x so the types describe the Node runtime actually pinned above. Types for a different major than the runtime is a correctness problem, not a cosmetic one.

jvm_test_dependencies.note: Test-scope only; never linked into a shipped artefact. Declared per AGENTS.md Sec. 3.

modules.why: Reads the committed vector files in the Java conformance runner; the JDK ships no JSON parser.
JUnit 5, the framework TRS Sec. 18.4 names for this module.
modules.licence_note: Weak copyleft limited to the library's own files. Test-only and not distributed; flagged explicitly because EPL is copyleft-family.

runtime_dependencies.note: Dependencies LINKED INTO A SHIPPED ARTEFACT. Distinct from build_dependencies and jvm_test_dependencies, which never reach a user, and the distinction matters most for licences: a copyleft build tool imposes nothing, a copyleft runtime dependency imposes its terms on what is distributed. Every entry here must also appear in docs/legal/third-party-notices.md, which the app ships.

modules.why: Argon2id for the ADR-003 RecoveryRecord. The JCA has no Argon2 at any API level, so there is no platform alternative; it also supplies ChaCha20-Poly1305, which the JCA provides only from API 28 while minSdk is 26. Bundles libsodium (ISC) in binary form for four ABIs.
modules.licence_note: THE FIRST COPYLEFT DEPENDENCY THIS PROJECT SHIPS. MPL-2.0 is file-scoped: used unmodified it places no obligation on Lumos sources. Owner-approved 2026-08-18 with conditions; see not_yet_pinned.resolved_in_s4b.
modules.licence_verification: The shipped AAR carries NO licence file - the MPL-2.0 declaration is in the POM and in the upstream repository's LICENSE.md, and the notices file reproduces the text from the latter. Recorded because the adoption condition said to read the licence from the shipped artefact, and the shipped artefact does not carry one.
modules.raised_in: WP-02 slice S5, executing CR-002. Held at 5.1.0 through S4b and S4c because 5.2.0 ships bytecode-65 class files that a Java 17 javac refuses; the Java 21 toolchain removes that.
modules.alignment_verified: Read from the artefacts rather than from the release notes. Every PT_LOAD segment of the 64-bit objects in 5.2.0 has p_align 0x4000 (16 KB): jni/arm64-v8a/libsodium.so and jni/x86_64/libsodium.so. The same segments in 5.1.0 have p_align 0x1000 (4 KB), which is the defect - an Android 15 device with 16 KB pages cannot map that object at all. The 32-bit ABIs are unaffected by the rule. Android Lint Aligned16KB is consequently ENABLED again in android-app/app/build.gradle.kts and passing; the narrow disable that recorded the gap is deleted.
modules.abi_note: 5.2.0 drops the legacy armeabi ABI that 5.1.0 shipped. No supported device uses it and the module already declares abiFilters, so nothing changes in the APK.
modules.surface_unchanged: crypto_pwhash and the AEAD entry points LibsodiumRecoveryCrypto binds are identical across the bump. The evidence is the cross-language recovery vectors, re-executed on an emulator against 5.2.0 - 21 instrumented tests, including the four derivation KATs and the 16 negative cases - not the release notes.

modules.why: The native-call layer Lazysodium binds through. Declared explicitly, and the transitive excluded, because the POM asks for the JAR and Android needs the AAR variant that carries libjnidispatch.so.
modules.licence_note: Dual-licensed at the user's option; Lumos takes Apache-2.0 and reproduces that text in the notices file. The LGPL option is not exercised.

swiftpm_dependencies.note: SwiftPM packages, pinned twice: `exact:` in Package.swift and an immutable revision in Package.resolved. Swift does not exist on the authoring host, so Package.resolved was authored from the upstream tag's commit rather than produced by `swift package resolve`; the conformance workflow's swift job resolves and asserts the revision matches, which is what turns the claim into evidence.

modules.why: Argon2id for the iOS RecoveryRecord. CryptoKit has no Argon2; ChaCha20-Poly1305 still comes from CryptoKit, as it has since WP-01.
modules.scope: Only the Clibsodium product - the libsodium XCFramework and its module map. The package's Sodium Swift wrapper is NOT used: its PWHash.hash maps the password through Int8(_:), which traps on any byte above 0x7F, so a passphrase with an accent in it would crash rather than fail.
modules.licence_verification: LICENSE read from the 0.11.0 tag: ISC, Frank Denis. libsodium itself is ISC and its text is reproduced in the notices file.
